decisions.reason: The water phantom for particle therapy remains a specialized option with unresolved market demand, but keeping it costs little relative to the firm's commitment to particle therapy.
Small volume ionization chambers have become standard tools for small-field dosimetry, so their option value is high and keeping cost is low.
This second small volume chamber partially overlaps with Product B, raising the chance of pruning, but distinct clinical applications still justify keeping the option open.
The standard clinical chamber line is a core, revenue-generating product with proven market acceptance, so there is little reason to drop it.
Relative dosimetry chambers are mature and stable, requiring minimal additional investment, so the option is kept.
Thimble ionization chambers are a well-established product category with steady demand, making abandonment unlikely.
